land.text: Transcaucasia, governed from Tiflis by the Transcaucasian Commissariat (established 15 November 1917) and its Seim (23 February 1918) before the federation was proclaimed

predecessors.note: The Commissariat page: it 'declared independence from Soviet Russia and formed the TDFR'. The federation continues the Commissariat's government rather than replacing it, so no separate Commissariat dossier is written; Cliopatria's Russian Republic rows (1917-1919) are the only shapes that cover the land before 22 April 1918.

land.text: the Georgian members proclaimed the Democratic Republic of Georgia on 26 May 1918

capitals.name: Tiflis (Tbilisi)
capitals.note: Infobox capital Tbilisi (Tiflis); 'Tiflis was the seat of the viceroy and the region's de facto capital'.

correction.text: Transcaucasia as the Seim proclaimed it on 22 April 1918: 'most of the territory of present-day Armenia, Azerbaijan and Georgia' (the union of the three successors' Cliopatria 1918 shapes), with Kars (held until 25 April) added, and Batum (occupied by the Ottomans on 14 April) and Baku (held by the Baku Commune from 13 April) taken out

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no row for the federation, whose life (22 April-26/28 May 1918) falls inside the first year of its three successors' shapes. The page gives no area; the three successor shapes sum to about 174,000 km2 before overlaps (Georgia 70,484, Armenia 16,537, Azerbaijan Democratic Republic 87,458). The page says only that the state 'included most of the territory of present-day Armenia, Azerbaijan and Georgia' plus parts of Russia and Turkey, so the shape is a reading from the successors' outlines. The Baku subtraction (40 km) and the Batumi subtraction (45 km) are the researcher's radii for 'Bolsheviks controlling Baku' (TDFR page; the Baku Commune page gives 13 April-25 July 1918) and for Batum 'occupied on 14 April'; the Baku Commune has no dossier, and the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic's Cliopatria 1918 shape includes Baku, so a gap-filler should decide who held Baku before 28 May.

region.text: Transcaucasia as the Seim proclaimed it on 22 April 1918: 'most of the territory of present-day Armenia, Azerbaijan and Georgia' (the union of the three successors' Cliopatria 1918 shapes), with Kars (held until 25 April) added, and Batum (occupied by the Ottomans on 14 April) and Baku (held by the Baku Commune from 13 April) taken out

ledger.note: 1918, 22 April: the Seim proclaims Transcaucasia an independent federative republic at Tiflis. Page: Davit Oniashvili proposed the motion 'to proclaim Transcaucasia an independent democratic federative republic,' which passed with few dissents; infobox 'proclaimed on 22 April 1918'. The page names no frontier, so the region is the successors' 1918 outlines (see the keyframe). The Ottoman Empire recognised the federation on 28 April.

region.text: 'the territories of Ardahan, Batum Oblast, and Kars Oblast', ceded to the Ottomans at Brest-Litovsk and taken by them in April 1918

ledger.note: 1918, April: the Ottoman army holds Batum and presses on Kars. 'On 14 April the Seim declared war on the Ottoman Empire'; 'Batum was occupied on 14 April "with little resistance"'; Erzurum and Kars were occupied shortly after the declaration. The Ottoman army had crossed the 1914 frontier by 24 March (Caucasus campaign page). The federation refused the Brest-Litovsk cession of Ardahan, Batum and Kars, so the three oblasts are the zone.

region.text: Kars, the fortress city and oblast

ledger.note: 1918, 25 April: Kars is evacuated. 'Kars was held by Armenian forces until it was evacuated on 25 April'; the Caucasus campaign page has the Ottomans besieging it from 23 April and the surrender agreed on 25 April. The page does not say the garrison acted for the federation, so the region is the researcher's reading.

region.text: the Democratic Republic of Georgia as Cliopatria draws it for 1918

ledger.note: 1918, 26 May: the Seim dissolves and the Georgian members proclaim the Democratic Republic of Georgia. Page: 'the Seim certifies the fact of the dissolution of Transcaucasia and lays down its powers.' The same day, the Georgian members proclaimed the Democratic Republic of Georgia.

region.text: the Erivan lands of the Republic of Armenia as Cliopatria draws them for 1918

ledger.note: 1918, 28 May: Armenia declares independence, 'two days later' than 26 May. The Caucasus campaign page says Armenia and Azerbaijan declared independence 'on the same day' as Georgia (26 May); the two pages disagree and the TDFR page and the Armenian dossier's 28 May stand.

region.text: the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic as Cliopatria draws it for 1918

ledger.note: 1918, 28 May: Azerbaijan proclaims its independence the same day as Armenia. Baku, held by the Baku Commune until it fell in July 1918, is outside the land the federation held.

region.text: 'the territories of Ardahan, Batum Oblast, and Kars Oblast', ceded to the Ottomans at Brest-Litovsk and taken by them in April 1918

ledger.note: 1918, 26-28 May: the war passes to the successors. The Ottomans resumed their advance on 21 May and 'stalled at Bash Abaran, Sardarapat, and Kara Killisse'; the Treaty of Batum followed on 4 June (Caucasus campaign page). The page gives no end to the federation's own contest, so the end is bridged to its dissolution.

region.text: Transcaucasia, divided among the Democratic Republic of Georgia, the Republic of Armenia and the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic

ledger.note: 1918, 26-28 May: the federation ends. Infobox 'Dissolution: 28 May 1918'; the Seim itself dissolved on 26 May; successors 'Democratic Republic of Georgia, Azerbaijan Democratic Republic, Republic of Armenia'.

wars.name: Caucasus campaign

zones.text: 'the territories of Ardahan, Batum Oblast, and Kars Oblast', ceded to the Ottomans at Brest-Litovsk and taken by them in April 1918

wars.outcome: Ottoman victory on the ground: Batum taken on 14 April, Kars surrendered on 25 April; the offensive resumed on 21 May stalled at Sardarabad, Bash Abaran and Kara Killisse; the federation dissolved on 26-28 May and its successors signed the Treaty of Batum on 4 June.
wars.note: Only the 1918 phase of the Caucasus campaign (federation against the Ottomans, 14 April-28 May). The TDFR page states that 'the Seim declared war on the Ottoman Empire' on 14 April.

certainty.note: No frontier of the federation was fixed by treaty: the Brest-Litovsk cession of Ardahan, Batum and Kars was refused, the Trabzon and Batum conferences produced only a draft, and the outlines are the successors' Cliopatria shapes.

sources.title: Transcaucasian Democratic Federative Republic
sources.note: Identity, capital, 22 April proclamation, territory, Ottoman occupation of Batum and Kars, war declaration, dissolution 26-28 May, successors. No area in the infobox.

sources.title: Transcaucasian Commissariat
sources.note: Predecessor: established at Tiflis 15 November 1917; 'declared independence from Soviet Russia and formed the TDFR'. Thin: no territory, no area.

sources.title: Baku Commune
sources.note: Baku held by Bolsheviks 13 April-25 July 1918 (the page also says 26 July); does not mention the Seim or the federation.

sources.title: Caucasus campaign
sources.note: 1918 section: Brest-Litovsk 3 March, Ottoman crossing 24 March, Batum 14 April, Kars 23-25 April, Sardarabad/Bash Abaran/Kara Killisse 21-29 May, Treaty of Batum 4 June. Says Armenia and Azerbaijan declared independence on 26 May, against the TDFR page's 28 May.

notes: Cliopatria has no row for the federation; its three successors' 1918 shapes begin in the year it ended. A federation of 22 April-26/28 May 1918 shows on a yearly map only as the three successors' joint outline. Rulers omitted: the TDFR page names Nikolai Chkheidze (Seim chairman) and Akaki Chkhenkeli (prime minister) but no reign dates. Native names omitted: none of the pages opened gives one (Russian 'Zakavkazskaya Demokraticheskaya Federativnaya Respublika', Georgian and Armenian forms are known but were not read on a page). Not written: the Transcaucasian Commissariat/Seim phase (15 Nov 1917-22 April 1918), whose land Cliopatria draws as Russian Republic; the Baku Commune (13 April-25 July 1918), a state with no dossier and no Cliopatria row, whose land the keyframe leaves out of the federation. Disagreement: the Caucasus campaign page dates Armenia's and Azerbaijan's independence to 26 May, the TDFR page to 28 May. Gazetteer: all names used resolve (place Batumi, place Baku, admin1 Kars, Ardahan).
